clue.text: Whips bloke boxing one with conviction

indicators.note: a boxer's arms wrap round an opponent in a clinch, so the bloke here holds the next piece inside him

blocks.note: informal word for a man
an old lag is a convict, someone with a criminal conviction

explanation.surface: A man in a boxing ring takes on an opponent who has a criminal record, and whips him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with conviction' sounds like a person of firm belief, but an old lag is British slang for a habitual convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagella are the long whiplike threads that bacteria and sperm cells use for swimming.

clue.text: Open up one with sharp blow

blocks.note: dialect or French-style 'un' for one, as in 'a good un'
W is the standard abbreviation for with
a rap is a quick hard knock

explanation.surface: A boxer opens up his attack, landing a single sharp punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwrap a parcel is to take off its covering, which opens it up for the contents.

clue.text: Allow to get into round: it could be for the better

definitions.text: it could be for the better

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so the allow word sits within the round word

blocks.note: a round, as in a milk or paper round, is a regular route
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A boxer is told to go into the next round, which might turn things in his favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the better' reads as 'to improve matters', but 'better' here is one who bets: roulette is a game played by gamblers.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game, so it is something laid on for a bettor, a person placing wagers.

clue.text: Perhaps a cockney chicken: we hear one shouting

blocks.note: first meaning: a coward is yellow, which a Londoner of the East End would say with a dropped ending
second meaning: someone who yells

explanation.surface: Somebody shouting about a cockney who lost his nerve in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent turns 'yellow' (cowardly) into YELLER; the same word is literally someone who yells.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken and yellow are both slang for cowardly, and the cockney accent pronounces yellow with an -er ending.

clue.text: Annoying large one, entering place for fight

indicators.note: the pair of small pieces go into the fighting venue, ending up inside it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the Roman numeral for one
a boxing ring is where the fight happens

explanation.surface: A big fighter climbing into the ring is getting on everyone's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Riling someone is irritating or provoking them, the present participle of rile, so it works as an adjective here.

clue.text: Round Three over, finally getting the bell

indicators.note: finally points at the tail end of each of the two words just before it

blocks.note: a ring is a round shape
the closing letter of each word

explanation.surface: At the end of round three the bell sounds and the fight is over.
explanation.walkthrough: In the boxing picture 'Round' and 'the bell' belong together, but 'Round' is the ring shape and 'the bell' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is something that rings, so it can be called a ringer, as can a person who rings church bells.

clue.text: Turn to corner to fix things

blocks.note: to do a job, or do up a house, is to fix it
gear means belongings or kit

explanation.surface: A boxer's cornerman turns to his corner to sort out the equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' sits between definition and wordplay but belongs to the definition: folding a page turns its tip into a corner flap.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog-ear a book is to fold down the top corner of a page as a bookmark.

clue.text: Flamboyant jumper worn by short male

indicators.note: something short is missing its last bit, so the male bird loses its final letter
clothes worn by someone are around them, so the jumper surrounds the shortened bird

blocks.note: a kangaroo, the jumping animal
a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A short man wearing a garishly colourful sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, as Britons call a pullover; here it is the kangaroo, ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the highly ornate eighteenth-century style of art and decoration, so the word describes anything extravagantly showy.

clue.text: Clobber in ring? One packing punches around top of ribs

indicators.note: the top of a word written downward is its first letter
the punches word goes round the outside of the single letter

blocks.note: someone who packs things into boxes
shots are blows or punches
first letter

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring lands hits round his opponent's ribs.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes, not a verb for hitting. 'One packing punches' wants to be a boxer who packs a punch; the boxer is someone packing boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose underpants modelled on the trunks boxers wear, hence clothing for the ring.

clue.text: Fury's leader at the end: previously put on ass

indicators.note: the leading letter is sent to the back, so the word rotates by one place

blocks.note: taken as written
rage is fury

explanation.surface: Tyson Fury, the heavyweight boxer, ends up ahead after earlier being taken for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fury's' is 'Fury is': rage. 'Previously put' places the small word in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of Asia, a relative of the donkey.

clue.text: They're put down on canvas? Beat one that's run out of craft in the main?

definitions.text: one that's run out of craft in the main?

blocks.note: oil paints are applied to a canvas; oils are also the paintings
to lick an opponent is to beat them

explanation.surface: Boxers knocked onto the canvas, beaten, and one left without any skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The canvas is the ring floor and 'run out of craft' sounds like losing skill; in fact the canvas is an artist's, and the craft is a ship at sea, the main.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil slick is a film of oil spilled from a tanker or other vessel, leaking out across the open sea.

clue.text: Fully fit

blocks.note: first meaning: thoroughly
second meaning: healthy

explanation.definitionFit: The word means thoroughly as an adverb (well done) and in good health as an adjective (feeling well).

clue.text: Frame of other picture shot round island

indicators.note: a frame is the border of a picture, so only the edge letters of the word are kept
something shot is ruined or wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: first and last letters
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A photo of a different scene, framed, taken around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerto Rico is a Caribbean island, a self-governing territory of the United States.

clue.text: Ungracefully fleshy: admit being out of shape

indicators.note: letters that are out of shape have lost their proper form and must be reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy, overweight boxer owning up to being unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham-fisted, with fists like hams, fits a boxer, and so does 'out of shape'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ham-fisted means clumsy with the hands, so doing something that way is doing it awkwardly, without grace.

clue.text: Fury's beginning to swell after punch that's light

indicators.note: the beginning of the name is its opening letter only

blocks.note: first letter
to lam is to hit hard
a swell is a dandy, a smartly dressed man, as is a beau

explanation.surface: Tyson Fury's face starts to puff up after taking a punch, a light one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like a verb for bruising; it is the old noun for a fashionable man. 'After' puts the swell behind the punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, a source of light, from the French for flame.

clue.text: Plant left one at the close to seal a victory

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
V for victory
one who ends something, who is there at its close

explanation.surface: A boxer's left in the closing seconds clinches the win.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in the clue's order, 'one at the close' comes first, but it goes last: it seals, or completes, the 'a victory' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant shrub with purple flower spikes, grown in gardens and for its oil.

clue.text: Long right jabs this close to heavyweight

indicators.note: a jab pokes into something, so the single letter is pushed inside the next word
the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
last letter

explanation.surface: A long right-hand punch lands close to a heavyweight boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long right' reads as a long punch, but 'Long' is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave it, and to thirst after it is the same strong desire.

clue.text: Damaged and knocked out when caught?

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so what matters is the word as it is heard

blocks.note: a boxer knocked out is floored, sent to the floor

explanation.surface: A fighter hurt and knocked out after being caught by a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, where the r is silent, floored and flawed sound the same. 'Caught' looks like being hit, but it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed has a defect or blemish, so it is imperfect or damaged.

clue.text: Present a fight around that time

blocks.note: someone present is there
taken as written
a bout is a boxing match

explanation.surface: Someone gives a boxing match round about that time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereabout means near that point, approximately, used of a place, number or time.

clue.text: I can't wait for rumble that's taking place

blocks.note: a roll of thunder or drums is a rumble
an event that is on is happening

explanation.surface: An eager fan can't wait for the big fight, the rumble, to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumble' suggests the boxing match, as in the Rumble in the Jungle, but it is just a rolling sound.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Roll on the weekend!' is an idiom of eager impatience, wishing a future event would arrive soon.

clue.text: Ripped: topless professional fighter in ring

indicators.note: without its top, the word written downward loses its first letter

blocks.note: ripped and tore are both past tense of tearing
short form of professional

explanation.surface: A muscular, shirtless professional boxer in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripped' looks like muscular and 'topless' like bare-chested; the ring is a bullring, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is a bullfighter, especially one on foot, who fights in the circular bullring arena.

clue.text: Governor-general against boxing legend

blocks.note: V for versus, against
Muhammad Ali, the great heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: A senior official squaring up against a famous boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like a container signal, but here it just describes the legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A vali was the governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire, a regional ruler appointed by the sultan.

clue.text: Training part that's boring

blocks.note: drill is repetitive training, as for soldiers
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A dull section of a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means dull in the surface; the definition means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill bit is the cutting tool fitted to a drill, the thing that bores holes.

clue.text: Some adventure now needed for glory

indicators.note: some of means only a portion of the phrase that follows, a run of its letters

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A little adventure is now necessary to win fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame and wide acclaim, which is what glory means in the sense of honour won.

clue.text: Hard men punching to weaken part of the torso

indicators.note: a punch drives into its target, so the first pieces go inside the weaken word

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
other ranks, ordinary soldiers
to tax someone is to strain or tire them

explanation.surface: Tough fighters landing blows to the body to wear an opponent down.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the crossword's usual term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest region, between neck and abdomen, the upper part of the trunk.

clue.text: Father and I with close acquaintance

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
taken as written
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A priest and the speaker, along with a close friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close acquaintance' reads as one phrase, but 'close' is wordplay and 'acquaintance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend is a person one knows and likes; an acquaintance is anyone one knows, so the two overlap loosely.
